chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Musa (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated to us, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Farsi, from Abu Hanifa Muhammad ibn Yahya, from al-Walid ibn Aban, from Muhammad ibn Abdillah ibn Miskan, from his father, who said: Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:

Indeed Fatimah bint Asad (may Allah have mercy on her) came to Abu Talib to give him the good news of the birth of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family). So Abu Talib said to her: 'Be patient with me for a Saturday, I will come to you with something similar, except for prophethood.' He said: 'The Saturday is thirty years.' And there were thirty years between the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him).

key_terms.أَبُو طَالِبٍ: Abu Talib, uncle of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW)
key_terms.فَاطِمَةُ بِنْتُ أَسَدٍ: Fatimah bint Asad, mother of Imam Ali (AS)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the 'Saturday' mentioned in the hadith of Fatimah bint Asad?
ai.summary: This narration from *Mani al-Akhbar* highlights the unique status of Fatimah bint Asad, the mother of Imam Ali, by linking her joy at the Prophet's birth to the subsequent thirty-year period of Imam Ali's life. In Shia scholarship, this interval is often interpreted as the time Imam Ali spent in the Prophet's lap, symbolizing his intimate spiritual and physical upbringing under the Prophet's direct care. The hadith thus reinforces the concept of *Nubuwwah* (prophethood) and *Imamah* (leadership) as closely intertwined, with Ali serving as the living embodiment of the Prophet's legacy during those formative years.
